Title: How CMTF obtains its causal path is unverified
What is open (description): ToolMenuBench's best method (CMTF, 85.7% at 1,125 tokens) is described as using 'the next causally necessary action'; whether it uses information a deployed policy would not have is not verified.
What is known now: ToolMenuBench tasks are 'defined by a user request, an initial symbolic state, a goal state, and a gold tool trajectory', run in a deterministic mocked environment (EXT-0166); each method receives 'the same task, current symbolic state, goal condition, and tool registry' (EXT-0148); CMTF exposes only the next causally necessary frontier (EXT-0148). GIST-CMTF tasks include candidate goals, an intended goal and a gold tool path, with a 'Gold-goal CMTF: applies CMTF using the annotated intended goal' upper-bound baseline; its goal-inference module takes the request, the current symbolic state and tool contracts (formal definition) (EXT-0179); GIST-CMTF states CMTF 'assumes that the user request has already been mapped to a symbolic goal state', 'often unrealistic' (EXT-0139). Not stated in the ranges read: who authored the contracts; whether CMTF receives the annotated goal at run time in ToolMenuBench; how goal inference is implemented in the experiments. Batch 9: in ToolMenuBench each instance includes an annotated goal state and the filter maps 'task, current state, goal, and registry' to a visible subset; the next frontier comes from the goal, the current symbolic state and manually specified contracts, so the goal is given, not inferred (EXT-0206, EXT-0207). The stored r2 text is GIST-CMTF, a follow-up, not the CMTF paper; it states that CMTF 'assumes that the user request has already been mapped to a symbolic goal state' and that 'even accurate contracts still require a target goal state' (EXT-0208); GIST-CMTF infers the goal among a controlled candidate-goal set: gold-goal oracle 99.5% success, GIST-CMTF 97.0%, top-goal CMTF 80.1%, semantic-goal 82.9%, all tools 53.5% (a different task suite from ToolMenuBench's 32.1%, not comparable). On deployment the texts give only assumptions and limitations (a shared symbolic vocabulary, synthetic tasks, mocked execution, 'do not directly measure latency, monetary cost'), no deployment evidence. The original CMTF paper (arXiv 2606.06284) was not examined.
Closed when: Closed 2026-10-19: the stored texts say how the causal path is obtained; the brief's 'suggests it uses information a deployed policy would not have' is consistent with them.
Status basis (evidence pointer): FND-0025 (findings/SUM-0027); EXT-0205, EXT-0206, EXT-0207, EXT-0208
Decision / result (on closure): Closed 2026-10-19: CMTF uses an annotated goal state in ToolMenuBench (given, not inferred); GIST-CMTF infers it among candidates; no deployment evidence.
